In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of the nuclear dynamics with impact parameter in heavy-ion collisions.
the evolution of the reaction mechanism from binary collisions to a fusion process.
the study of a fusionlike process, in which the system is formed at a very high density and a large temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fusionlike process is not an exclusive mode of the collision.
a fusionlike system is formed in the 32 MeV/ nucleon {sup 58Ni+58}Ni reaction.
the 32 MeV/N collisions between two {sup 58Ni} nuclei are neither a simple fusionlike reaction nor a binary collision, but rather a complex process that is a mixture of both.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fusionlike process, with a large number of fragments and particles emitted in a short time, can be observed in heavy-ion collisions at energies well below the barrier.
the fusionlike process is a single-source emission, which can be described by a statistical model.

the decay of a fusionlike compound system is a complex process that involves the interplay between several mechanisms, including the preformation of fragments and particles, and a coexistence between two decay modes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a duality exists between two decay modes of a single source, which can be interpreted as a signature of a fusionlike process.
the fusionlike process is not a simple extension of the binary process.
the fusionlike system, although it has a lifetime of a few 10{sup -22} s, can be considered a compound nucleus.
